response.rationale: The linear, depressed forehead-to-scalp furrow with alopecia is characteristic of linear morphea (en coup de sabre), supported by lymphocytic perifollicular infiltrates with lobular panniculitis and hyaline fat necrosis. Negative ANA/anti-dsDNA, absent systemic features, and DIF deposition in dermal blood vessels rather than the basement membrane zone favor morphea over DLE. LPP is less likely because it lacks this deep linear furrow and subcutaneous panniculitis.

rejected.why: DLE would more typically show discoid scaling, follicular plugging, interface dermatitis, and basement-membrane-zone DIF; the linear depressed groove, dermal blood vessel deposition, and negative serologic tests are less supportive.
Lichen planopilaris causes perifollicular scarring alopecia but does not explain the depressed linear forehead groove, lobular panniculitis, or hyaline fat necrosis.
